question: How do I file an FIR?
answer: To file an FIR (First Information Report) in India: 1) Go to the nearest police station or use online portal; 2) Provide details of the incident including date, time, place, and description; 3) The police must register the FIR under Section 154 CrPC - they cannot refuse for cognizable offences; 4) You will receive a free copy of the FIR; 5) Note down the FIR number for future reference. You can also file Zero FIR at any police station if the crime occurred in a different jurisdiction.

question: What should I do if I witness a murder?
answer: If you witness a murder: 1) Immediately call police emergency number 100 or 112; 2) Do not tamper with the crime scene; 3) Do not touch any objects or evidence; 4) Note down important details - time, people involved, any identifying features; 5) Provide your statement to the police when they arrive; 6) You may be called as a witness during trial; 7) Under Section 176 CrPC, you have a legal duty to report such serious crimes. Contact victim compensation authorities for support.

question: What to do if someone is murdered in front of me?
answer: If someone is murdered in your presence: 1) Call emergency services immediately (dial 100 for police, 108 for ambulance); 2) Ensure your own safety first; 3) Do not disturb the crime scene; 4) Provide first aid to victim if safe and you know how; 5) Remember details about the perpetrator; 6) Give your statement to police - this makes you an eyewitness under Section 161 CrPC; 7) Police will record your statement; 8) You may need to testify in court. Under Indian law, you have both a civic and legal duty to report such crimes.

question: How to register a police complaint?
answer: To register a police complaint in India: 1) Visit the police station with jurisdiction over the area where incident occurred; 2) Explain your complaint verbally or in writing; 3) For cognizable offences, police must register FIR under Section 154 CrPC; 4) For non-cognizable offences, NCR (Non-Cognizable Report) is registered; 5) You can also file online complaints on state police websites; 6) Get acknowledgment receipt with complaint/FIR number; 7) If police refuse to register, you can approach Superintendent of Police or file complaint under Section 156(3) in Magistrate Court.

question: What are the steps to file FIR online?
answer: Steps to file FIR online: 1) Visit your state police website (e.g., Delhi Police, Mumbai Police portal); 2) Look for 'e-FIR' or 'Online Complaint' section; 3) Register/Login with mobile number; 4) Select complaint category and type of offence; 5) Fill in incident details - date, time, place, description; 6) Attach supporting documents if any; 7) Submit the form; 8) You will receive acknowledgment with reference number; 9) Note: Not all states offer online FIR for all types of crimes; 10) For serious crimes, physical presence may still be required. Print the acknowledgment for your records.

question: Can police refuse to file FIR?
answer: No, police cannot refuse to file FIR for cognizable offences. According to Section 154 CrPC: 1) Police are legally bound to register FIR for cognizable offences; 2) Refusal to register FIR is misconduct; 3) If police refuse, you can: a) Send written complaint by post to Superintendent of Police; b) File complaint under Section 156(3) before Judicial Magistrate; c) Approach State Human Rights Commission; d) File writ petition in High Court; 4) You have the right to get a free copy of FIR; 5) Police can refuse NCR for non-cognizable offences but must record it.

question: What is the difference between FIR and complaint?
answer: Difference between FIR and Complaint: FIR (First Information Report): 1) Registered for cognizable offences (serious crimes like murder, rape, theft); 2) Police can arrest without warrant; 3) Investigation starts immediately; 4) Filed under Section 154 CrPC at police station; 5) Free copy provided. COMPLAINT: 1) For non-cognizable offences (minor offences); 2) Registered as NCR (Non-Cognizable Report); 3) Police need Magistrate permission for arrest; 4) Investigation starts after Magistrate order; 5) Can be filed directly to Magistrate under Section 200 CrPC. FIR is for serious crimes requiring immediate action, Complaint is for less serious matters.

question: What should I do if someone threatens to kill me?
answer: If someone threatens to kill you: 1) Take the threat seriously - do not ignore; 2) Immediately file FIR under Section 506 IPC (Criminal intimidation) and Section 507 if threat is anonymous; 3) Collect evidence - save messages, recordings, emails, witnesses; 4) Apply for anticipatory bail if you fear false case; 5) Request police protection if threat is serious; 6) You can approach Magistrate under Section 156(3) if police don't act; 7) Apply for restraining order; 8) Inform family and workplace about threat; 9) Consider changing location temporarily. Criminal intimidation is punishable with up to 7 years imprisonment. Your safety is paramount - act immediately.

question: How to report domestic violence?
answer: To report domestic violence in India: 1) Call Women Helpline 181 (24x7); 2) File complaint at nearest police station under Domestic Violence Act 2005; 3) File FIR for physical abuse under IPC Sections 498A, 323, 325, 307; 4) Approach Protection Officer appointed by government; 5) File petition before Magistrate under Section 12 of DV Act for protection order; 6) You can claim: a) Protection order to stop violence; b) Residence order to stay in shared household; c) Monetary relief; d) Custody of children; e) Compensation; 7) Free legal aid available; 8) Counseling centers available; 9) Contact NGOs for support. You do not need to leave the house - law protects your right to shared household.

question: What to do after a road accident?
answer: Steps after a road accident: 1) Stop immediately - leaving is a crime under Section 187 IPC; 2) Call emergency: 108 for ambulance, 100 for police; 3) Provide first aid to injured if safe; 4) Do not move vehicles until police arrive (except for traffic clearance); 5) Take photos/videos of accident scene, vehicle damage, injuries; 6) Exchange information with other party - license, insurance, contact; 7) Note down witness details; 8) File FIR/police report within 24 hours; 9) Inform insurance company immediately; 10) Get medical examination even for minor injuries; 11) Preserve medical bills for compensation; 12) Do not admit fault or sign any documents without legal advice. Under Motor Vehicles Act, you can claim compensation.
